judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's mathematical claims are correct - -4 x (-2) = 8 so 6 > -2 becomes -24 < 8; -4x > 12 gives x < -3; -7x <= 21 gives x >= -3; -x/3 < 2 gives x > -6; -5(-4) - 2 = 18; 4 - 3x > 19 gives x < -5; 8 - 2x >= 14 gives x <= -3 - and problem 8 is correctly declared manual. But 'ACCEPT, 32/32' with answer_key_quality 4/4 and visual_and_print_quality 4/4 cannot stand against page 1 of the delivered answer key, which I rendered and read directly. The Quick Answers bank prints:  '2. -inf, -3, ibuilt-in function openi',  '4. -6, inf, ibuilt-in function openi',  '6. -inf, -5, ibuilt-in function openi'.  That is the repr of the Python builtin open() typeset into a teacher-facing PDF, with its angle brackets rendered as inverted punctuation by the default OT1 encoding. I reproduced the mechanism exactly: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies each string element of an inequality expected triple, sympy.sympify('open') returns <built-in function open>, and sympy.latex of that returns \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}. 'closed' happens to become a Symbol and renders cleanly, which is why row 3 and row 7 look plausible and only three rows are visibly broken. Even setting the garbage aside, the bank renders solution sets as a raw endpoint triple rather than the 'x < -3' the worked key boxes and the student is asked to write, so three of the seven machine-checked answers are unusable for at-a-glance grading. Separately, the sheet declares only one manual item while problems 3(b) ('Name her error in one sentence') and 7(a) ('Which of Dev's two steps is wrong, and why is the other one fine?') are also open responses, and problems 1, 3 and 7 print more responses than verify.json covers. The judge stated it independently checked the artifacts; a Python builtin's repr on page 1 of the answer key is not consistent with a perfect score on answer-key and print quality.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 1 makes the rule observable instead of asserting it: start from the true statement 6 > -2, multiply both sides by -4, then compare -24 with 8 and report what '>' became. Every later solve on the sheet refers back to that experience, and the declared trap (-8, from keeping the sign of the first factor) catches the arithmetic slip that would sabotage it.

Problem 5 is a boundary check rather than another solve - substitute x = -4 into -5x - 2 and confirm 18 - and the stem pre-names the wrong answer a sign error produces ('A student who gets -22 here has broken the negative-times-negative rule'). It teaches self-checking as a step.

The directions make the flip visible in the student's own work ('When you divide or multiply by a negative, write flip beside that step'), and the answer key's display equations print a small 'flip' label over the relation symbol at exactly the step where it turns around.
Problem 8 IS correctly declared as a manual verify entry with a specific description of what a human must read - the pattern the rest of this shard should follow.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt routes every string 'expected' through sympy.sympify. For an inequality problem the expected value is an endpoint/closure triple containing the literal 'open', and sympify resolves that name to the Python builtin open(), which sympy.latex renders as \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}. Nothing downstream validates that a sympify result is a SymPy object, so a Python internal is typeset into the delivered answer key. The same helper's SympifyError branch silently degrades relation answers to '---' elsewhere in this run, so both failure modes come from one unguarded sympify call.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-184/answer_key.pdf page 1, Quick Answers rows 2, 4 and 6 print 'ibuilt-in function openi' (confirmed by rendering the page, not only by text extraction)
evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-184/verify.json ids 2, 4 and 6 declare expected triples ending in the literal 'open'
Reproduced directly: sympy.sympify('open') -> <built-in function open>; sympy.latex(...) -> \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt(): the str branch sympifies unconditionally and only guards SympifyError/SyntaxError/TypeError/ValueError, not a non-SymPy result

root_causes.description: Items that require a written diagnosis or a drawn representation are recorded as machine verified because a numeric companion value exists, so the gate log reports zero manual items for a sheet full of open responses. The manual type exists and is used correctly on other cases in this same run, which shows the contract is author discretion rather than an enforced rule.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-184/worksheet.pdf problem 3(b) 'Name her error in one sentence' and problem 7(a) 'Which of Dev's two steps is wrong, and why is the other one fine?'
evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-184/verify.json declares exactly one manual entry (id 8); ids 3 and 7 are inequality entries only
evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-184/gate_log.txt: '7 passed, 0 failed, 1 manual' for a sheet with three explanation items

root_causes.description: The verify JSON is authored one entry per problem id rather than one entry per printed response, so a stem that asks for two things is recorded as fully machine verified when only its last component was checked. Nothing in the gate chain compares the number of answer locations the sheet prints against the number of entries covering them.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-184/worksheet.pdf problem 1 asks the student to circle the symbol that makes the new statement true and then to say what the original '>' became; verify.json id 1 checks only -4 x (-2) = 8

evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-184/worksheet.pdf problems 3 and 7 each print three lettered parts (a), (b), (c) under one Answer line, and verify.json covers only (c) in each case

improvements.title: Stop pushing relation symbols and interval keywords through sympify in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: render_quick_answers._fmt calls sympy.sympify on every string 'expected' and renders whatever comes back. Two vocabularies are not expressions and must be handled before that call. First, relation strings ('<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=') from compare problems raise SympifyError and degrade to the '---' the module documents as meaning 'manual, see solution', so a verified answer is advertised as unavailable. Second, the endpoint and closure triple of an inequality problem contains the literal 'open', which sympify resolves to the Python builtin open() and sympy.latex renders as \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}. Render relations verbatim as math, render an inequality triple as the solution the student writes (x < -3) or as standard interval notation, never sympify the literals open/closed/oo/-oo, and make a sympify result that is not a SymPy object a hard error rather than a rendered repr.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_render_quick_answers.py, render a bank from a verify JSON containing {"id": 2, "type": "inequality", "expr": "-4*x - 12", "relation": ">", "expected": ["-oo", -3, "open"]} and assert the rendered text contains neither 'built-in function' nor 'mathtt', and does contain the student-facing form '$x < -3$'. Both assertions fail on today's _fmt, which emits \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}, and pass once inequality triples are formatted without sympify.
improvements.expected_impact: The at-a-glance grading bank stops printing Python internals into a teacher-facing PDF and stops blanking out every comparison answer on comparison-heavy sheets, where today it can be more than half empty.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is confined to one formatting helper, and the fixture-locked invariant that bank entries stay plain text outside \ans and \boxed is untouched.

improvements.title: Declare a manual verify entry for every explain, name-the-error, or draw-it item
improvements.proposed_change: Any problem whose stem asks the student to explain, justify, say why, name the error, describe, decide which student is right, or draw and label a representation must carry a 'manual' entry in verify.json alongside whatever numeric entries it also needs. Add a lint over the \problem stems in the worksheet tex that flags those constructions and fails the build when the matching problem id has no manual entry, so 'N passed, 0 manual' can only be printed by a sheet that genuinely contains no open response.
improvements.regression_test: Add a lint fixture from curr-184 problems 3 and 7 ('Name her error in one sentence', 'Which of Dev's two steps is wrong, and why is the other one fine?') with a verify JSON that declares a manual entry only for problem 8. The lint must exit non-zero naming problems 3 and 7; declaring manual entries for them must clear it.
improvements.expected_impact: The gate log's manual count becomes a truthful statement about the sheet, and the prompt's standing instruction to clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review is satisfied structurally instead of by author discretion.
improvements.risk: Verb matching will over-trigger on rhetorical asides such as 'show your thinking' in the directions block. Scope the scan to \problem stems and allow an explicit per-problem acknowledgement flag to suppress a false positive.

improvements.title: Verify every response the worksheet prints a slot for, not only the final numeric result
improvements.proposed_change: Require one verify-JSON entry (machine or manual) per distinct response the sheet asks the student to write, not one per problem id. That covers each lettered sub-part, the remainder half of a 'quotient with a remainder' answer, the person or option a stem asks the learner to name, and every intermediate form a stem explicitly requests before the final one. Enforce it with a gate that counts printed answer locations per problem in the worksheet tex (\ansline, \ansblank, \answerline, and (a)/(b)/(c) part markers inside a \problem stem) and fails the build when a problem's combined machine plus manual entries cover fewer slots than the sheet prints.
improvements.regression_test: Extend the slot gate fixture with curr-184 problem 3, whose stem prints (a), (b) and (c) under one Answer line against a single inequality entry. The gate must report two uncovered responses until entries (machine for (a)'s substitution test, manual for (b)'s named error) are added.
improvements.expected_impact: Every printed blank has a checked value behind it, so neither the Quick Answers bank nor a boxed key answer can be a partial answer to the question actually asked.
improvements.risk: Counting slots from tex is heuristic and a stem that prints '(a)' as ordinary prose could raise a false failure. Scope the counter to part markers at the start of a sentence and allow an explicit per-problem slot-count override in the verify JSON.

case_summary: The mathematics, the misconception design and the study guide are all excellent, and problem 8 is the one item in this shard flagged manual exactly as it should be. But the delivered answer key prints '-inf, -3, ibuilt-in function openi' on page 1 for three of its eight problems - the repr of Python's open() leaking through an unguarded sympify call in the Quick Answers renderer. That is visible garbage in the artifact a teacher grades from, and it makes 32/32 with 4/4 on answer-key and print quality untenable; this is my clearest disagreement with the judge in the shard. Two lesser gaps compound it: the bank shows interval triples rather than the inequality the student writes, and problems 1, 3 and 7 print more responses (a substitution test, a named error, a circled symbol) than verify.json covers.
